messages:
emily: Hey team — running into 429s for a customer doing a demo. They’re on the free plan and hit a burst while loading ~1200 short prompts over 3 minutes. Repro steps below. Can we confirm if this is quota exhaustion or a bug?

emily: repro (sanitized):
```bash
curl -i -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate \n  -H \"Authorization: Bearer sk-live-REDACTED\" \n  -H \"Content-Type: application/json\" \n  -d '{"model":"redwood-alpha-1","input":"hello"}'
```
Response headers snippet: 
```
HTTP/1.1 429 Too Many Requests
x-rate-limit-limit: 60
x-rate-limit-remaining: 0
x-rate-limit-reset: 1718923500
x-request-id: demo-abc-123
```
Body: `{\"error\":\"quota_exceeded\", \"message\":\"Burst quota exhausted for account\"}`

emily: Customer says they expected short burst capacity during demos. They tried backing off and saw requests succeed after ~1m. Need a short-term fix for this demo tomorrow. :grimacing:

sam (support): Thanks Emily — this looks like classic free-tier burst exhaustion. Quick Qs: what’s the customer account id (or email) and the org plan shown in Console? I can do an immediate temporary lift if we have Sales signoff. Also please paste full x-request-id if you see more than one.

emily: Org id: org_9xQ-demo (DMing full account id / billing info). x-request-id: demo-abc-123 and demo-abc-124 for subsequent attempts. Console shows \"Free\" plan, usage spike ~ 3.2k tokens/min during demo.

RateLimiterBot: SYSTEM: Account org_9xQ-demo exceeded burst allowance. Auto-throttle enabled. Next refill in 62s.

sam (support): OK — free plan has a small token-bucket burst window (60 requests/min baseline in this region). We allow short bursts but sustained sequences of concurrent short requests deplete the bucket quickly. Workarounds:
- add exponential backoff (start 200ms) or jitter on client side
- batch prompts into one request where possible
- use embeddings/generate batching endpoints if demo allows

sam (support): If they need a guaranteed short-term increase, Sales can provision a temporary paid trial with reserved burst capacity or a one-off exception for <48h. @jason can you confirm process?

jason (sales): Yep — we can provision a 14–30 day trial with elevated limits (reserved small Dedicated pool) or grant a temporary quota exception for review. Need: org name, use-case (demo), expected TPS/req/min, and billing contact. I can do the exception for low-risk demos. I’ll take this offline — pinged @emily for details. :+1:

olivia (eng): From engineering: the rate limiter uses a token-bucket keyed by org + model family. When many parallel short requests hit, the bucket is drained faster than refill. We can raise the burst window for an org, but that’s a manual ops change and needs Sales approval and an audit entry. Alternative quick fix: route the demo traffic to a cheaper compatible model (e.g., redwood-lite-2) which has a separate quota and higher burst headroom.

olivia (eng): Diagnostics you can collect for us to make a targeted exception:
```
- full response headers (x-rate-limit-*) for a sample of failed + succeeding requests
- timestamps of the first 10 failures
- request payload sizes (avg tokens/request)
- customer account id and demo time window
```

emily: Thanks — I’ve DM’d the full account + billing contact to Sam and Jason. Customer agreed to route demo traffic to redwood-lite-2 for now if we can flip a flag. They want to avoid asking attendees to wait.

sam (support): I’ve created internal ticket S-2026-348 to track the exception request and linked the account. Escalating to Ops for a 48h soft-bump. @olivia can you review and approve ops changes?

olivia (eng): Saw the ticket. I can approve a 48h bump to the burst window (limited to this account + model family) once Sales confirms billing contact and we add an audit note. We’ll add a canary rule so we don’t affect cluster headroom.

jason (sales): Confirming billing contact and org details received. I’ll enable the trial path and request the temporary exception. I’ll follow up in-channel with the exception ID and duration.

emily: Great, thanks everyone. One more ask — can we add a small note to the product docs clarifying free-plan demo expectations and recommended client retry pattern? Several customers asked about this during onboarding. :thinking:

sam (support): Good call. Filed doc request DOC-889. Will draft a short blurb: \"Free plan includes limited burst capacity; for demos consider batching or a short paid trial\".

RateLimiterBot: ACTION: Temporary burst exception requested S-2026-348; pending Ops approval.

olivia (eng): Ops approved the canary bump. I applied a +2x burst window for org_9xQ-demo for 48h at 1718926800. Audit: olivia (eng) — temp-burst — reason: demo escalation.

sam (support): Closing loop — Emily, please confirm demo traffic succeeded after switching to redwood-lite-2 or once the bump applied. If anything breaks, DM me and I’ll reopen the ticket. :pray: 

emily: Confirmed — customer ran the demo 20m ago, traffic was smooth and no further 429s. They converted to a paid trial interest. Thank you all! :tada:
